arxiv-1808-05340.title: Genre-Agnostic Key Classification With Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-1808-05340.description: Abstract We propose modifications to the model structure and training procedure to a recently introduced Convolutional Neural Network for musical key classification. These modifications enable the network to learn a genre-independent model that performs better than models trained for specific music styles, which has not been the case in existing work.

arxiv-2104-03867.title: New X-ray observations of the hot subdwarf binary HD 49798/RX J0648.0–4418 2021
arxiv-2104-03867.creator: S. Mereghetti, F. Pintore, T. Rauch, N. La Palombara, P. Esposito, S. Geier, I. Pelisoli, M. Rigoselli, V. Schaffenroth, A. Tiengo
arxiv-2104-03867.description: Abstract HD 49798/RX J0648.0–4418 is the only confirmed X-ray binary in which the mass donor is a hot subdwarf star of O spectral type and, most likely, it contains a massive white dwarf (1.28 ± \pm 0.05 M ⊙ {\rm M}_{\odot} ) with a very fast spin period of 13.2 s.

arxiv-2204-06575.title: Discovery and analysis of three magnetic hot subdwarf stars: evidence for merger-induced magnetic fields 2022 Discovery and analysis of three magnetic hot subdwarf stars: evidence for merger-induced magnetic fields – 7
arxiv-2204-06575.creator: Ingrid Pelisoli, M. Dorsch, U. Heber, B. Gänsicke, S. Geier, T. Kupfer, P. Németh, S. Scaringi, V. Schaffenroth
arxiv-2204-06575.description: Abstract Magnetic fields can play an important role in stellar evolution. Among white dwarfs, the most common stellar remnant, the fraction of magnetic systems is more than 20 per cent. The origin of magnetic fields in white dwarfs, which show strengths ranging from 40 kG to hundreds of MG, is still a topic of debate.

arxiv-2206-09190.title: Dichroism in time-resolved ARPES and valence band orbital nature in BaNiS 2 \rm{BaNiS_{2}}
arxiv-2206-09190.creator: Jiuxiang Zhang, Zhesheng Chen, Jonathan Caillaux, Yannick Klein, Andrea Gauzzi, Azzedine Bendounan, Amina Taleb-Ibrahimi, Luca Perfetti, Evangelos Papalazarou, Marino Marsi
arxiv-2206-09190.description: Abstract Time-resolved ARPES gives access to the band structure and ultrafast dynamics of excited electronic states in solids. The orbital character of the bands close to the Fermi level is essential to understand the origin of several exotic phenomena in quantum materials.

arxiv-2212-05180.title: Dynamic Population Models with Temporal Preferential Sampling to Infer Phenology
arxiv-2212-05180.creator: Michael R. Schwob, Mevin B. Hooten, Travis McDevitt-Galles
arxiv-2212-05180.description: Abstract Abstract To study population dynamics, ecologists and wildlife biologists use relative abundance data, which are often subject to temporal preferential sampling. Temporal preferential sampling occurs when sampling effort varies across time. To account for preferential sampling, we specify a Bayesian hierarchical abundance model that considers the dependence between observation times and the ecological process of interest.

arxiv-2304-04895.title: From Disks to Channels: Dynamics of Active Nematics Confined to an Annulus
arxiv-2304-04895.creator: Chaitanya Joshi, Zahra Zarei, Michael M. Norton, Seth Fraden, Aparna Baskaran, Michael F. Hagan
arxiv-2304-04895.description: Abstract Confinement can be used to systematically tame turbulent dynamics occurring in active fluids. Although periodic channels are the simplest geometries to study confinement numerically, the corresponding experimental realizations require closed racetracks. Here, we computationally study 2D active nematics confined to such a geometry — an annulus.

arxiv-2406-12800.title: Supporting Human Raters with the Detection of Harmful Content using Large Language Models
arxiv-2406-12800.creator: Kurt Thomas, Patrick Gage Kelley, David Tao, Sarah Meiklejohn, Owen Vallis, Shunwen Tan, Blaž Bratanič, Felipe Tiengo Ferreira, Vijay Kumar Eranti, Elie Bursztein
arxiv-2406-12800.description: Abstract In this paper, we explore the feasibility of leveraging large language models (LLMs) to automate or otherwise assist human raters with identifying harmful content including hate speech, harassment, violent extremism, and election misinformation. Using a dataset of 50,000 comments, we demonstrate that LLMs can achieve 90% accuracy when compared to human verdicts.

arxiv-2503-13887.title: Strong quasi-MV* algebras and their logics
arxiv-2503-13887.creator: Lei Cai, Wenjuan Chen
arxiv-2503-13887.description: Abstract . In this paper, we introduce the subvariety of quasi-MV* algebras in order to characterize the logic which is related to complex fuzzy logic. First, we give the definitions of strong quasi-MV* algebra and strong quasi-Wajsberg* algebra and show that they are term equivalence. Second, we present the representation theorem and the standard completeness of strong quasi-MV* algebras.

arxiv-2507-08241.title: Exploring Gender Differences in Chronic Pain Discussions on Reddit
arxiv-2507-08241.creator: Ancita Maria Andrade, Tanvi Banerjee, Ramakrishna Mundugar
arxiv-2507-08241.description: Abstract Pain is an inherent part of human existence, manifesting as both physical and emotional experiences, and can be categorized as either acute or chronic. Over the years, extensive research has been conducted to understand the causes of pain and explore potential treatments, with contributions from various scientific disciplines.

arxiv-2507-12417.title: Spontaneous Spatial Cognition Emerges during Egocentric Video Viewing through Non-invasive BCI
arxiv-2507-12417.creator: Weichen Dai, Yuxuan Huang, Li Zhu, Dongjun Liu, Yu Zhang, Qibin Zhao, Andrzej Cichocki, Fabio Babiloni, Ke Li, Jianyu Qiu, Gangyong Jia, Wanzeng Kong, Qing Wu
arxiv-2507-12417.description: Abstract Humans possess a remarkable capacity for spatial cognition, allowing for self-localization even in novel or unfamiliar environments. While hippocampal neurons encoding position and orientation are well documented, the large-scale neural dynamics supporting spatial representation—particularly during naturalistic, passive experience—remain poorly understood.

pmc-10715183.title: The novel bacteriocin romsacin from Staphylococcus haemolyticus inhibits Gram-positive WHO priority pathogens
pmc-10715183.creator: Runa Wolden, Kirill V. Ovchinnikov, Hermoine J. Venter, Thomas F. Oftedal, Dzung B. Diep, Jorunn Pauline Cavanagh
pmc-10715183.description: Staphylococcus haemolyticus is an increasingly relevant nosocomial pathogen. The combination of multi-drug resistance and ability to form biofilms makes S. haemolyticus infections difficult to treat. Bacteriocins are ribosomally synthesized antimicrobial peptides produced by bacteria to inhibit growth of often closely related bacteria.

pmc-11261515.title: Étude des troubles anxiodépressifs chez les médecins de l’Institut de cancérologie « Salah Azaïez » de Tunis
pmc-11261515.creator: Imene Yeddes, Khadija Meddeb, Amina Mokrani, Imene Boukhris, Houyem Khiari
pmc-11261515.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). RESUMEIntroduction: Les oncologues sont souvent confrontés à des patients en fin de vie, souffrants. Cela peut générer un épuisement professionnel et des troubles anxio-dépressifs(TAD) pouvant altérer la qualité de vie des soignants.Objectif: Comparer le niveau des TAD chez les médecins exerçant à l’Institut Salah Azaïez (ISA) de Tunis par rapport à une population témoin de médecins qui ne prennent pas en charge la pathologie cancéreuse, en identifiant les éventuels facteurs associés à ces troubles.

pmc-11432625.title: Stimulatory Functions of Male Genitalia in Tipula (Triplicitipula) colei Alexander and Tipula (Lunatipula) translucida Doane (Diptera: Tipulidae) and Implications for Theories of Genital Evolution
pmc-11432625.creator: William G Eberhard, Jon K Gelhaus, Mariana F Wolfner
pmc-11432625.description: Simple SummaryThe morphological designs and the behavior (rhythmic brushing, vibrating, scraping, and tapping) of the male genitalia in two species of crane flies indicate that male genital structures in both species function to stimulate the female during copulation. These observations are used to test current theoretical explanations of the rapid divergent evolution of male genitalia of animals with internal insemination.

pmc-11513128.title: CDK4/6 inhibition initiates cell cycle arrest by nuclear translocation of RB and induces a multistep molecular response
pmc-11513128.creator: Ting Hong, Anna C Hogger, Dongbiao Wang, Qi Pan, Julie Gansel, Thomas Engleitner, Rupert Öllinger, Jürgen E Gschwend, Roland Rad, Roman Nawroth
pmc-11513128.description: CDK4/6 inhibitors are standard of care in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer. Treatment regimen consists of a combination with endocrine therapy, since their therapeutic efficacy as monotherapy in most clinical trials was rather limited. Thus, understanding the molecular mechanisms that underlie response to therapy might allow for the development of an improved therapy design.

pmc-11595896.title: Neuronal Intranuclear Inclusion Disease with a Corneal Disorder: A Case Report
pmc-11595896.creator: Mohamed Talaat Mohamed, Daisuke Inoue, Shunsuke Yoshimura, Masafumi Uematsu, Yasser Helmy Mohamed, Mao Kusano, Diya Tang, Akio Oishi, Takashi Kitaoka, Gou Takeo, Akihiro Ohira, Jack V Greiner, Stephen G Schwartz
pmc-11595896.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the formation of intranuclear inclusions in cells. Adult-type NIID usually develops in elderly patients with various clinical manifestations and is sometimes accompanied by ocular symptoms. A case of adult-onset NIID with early and unique manifestations, including a progressive corneal defect and retinal changes, which are concerning at a young age, is reported.

pmc-11606804.title: Hydrolyzed milk infant formula effectively protects against milk protein allergy: Independent of whey protein source
pmc-11606804.creator: Qinggang Xie, Sibo Liu, Dongying Cui, Yang Liu, Xiangxin Wang, Ting Cao, Xiaoxi Xu, Bailiang Li
pmc-11606804.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Milk protein sensitivity is a major challenge in infant feeding, especially for infants who cannot receive adequate breastfeeding. Hydrolyzed milk protein is a mainstream way to address this difficulty. The aim of this study was to assess the effect of differences in whey protein concentrate (WPC) source and the degree of hydrolysis on blocking allergy and to analyze the possible mechanisms by which hydrolyzed infant formula (IF) blocks allergy through colony‐metabolism–immunity response.

pmc-11656795.description: The plasma membrane is critical for the virulence of the human fungal pathogen Candida albicans. In addition to functioning as a protective barrier, the plasma membrane plays dynamic roles in a wide range of functions needed for virulence including nutrient uptake, cell wall synthesis, morphogenesis, resistance to stress, and invasive hyphal growth. pmc-12646065.title: Humanized DRAGA mice are a valuable model to study novel immunotherapies for HIV-1
pmc-12646065.creator: Pongthorn Pumtang-On, Liliana K Thron, Negin Goodarzi, Brianna C Davey, Emily N Sevcik, Natalie Coleman-Fuller, Ahmad F Karim, Vaiva Vezys, Mangala Rao, Branden S Moriarity, Mary S Pampusch, Aaron K Rendahl, Sofia A Casares, Pamela J Skinner
pmc-12646065.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Humanized (h) DRAGA mice are a promising in vivo model for investigating immunotherapies for treating HIV infections. These mice are not only susceptible to HIV infection, but they also develop functional human immune cells, including T cells and B cells, as well as follicular-like structures that mimic lymphoid B-cell follicles, where HIV-producing cells concentrate during infection in a manner similar to that found in humans.

pmc-12740756.title: Risk prediction models for malnutrition in cancer patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12740756.creator: Jiayan Yu, Xin Chu, Dongqing Guo, Wei Luo
pmc-12740756.description: BackgroundAlthough numerous models have been developed in recent years to predict malnutrition in cancer patients, their methodological rigor and clinical applicability remain uncertain. The lack of systematic evaluation hampers their integration into routine oncology and nursing practice, where early identification of at-risk patients is crucial for optimizing nutritional interventions, enhancing treatment tolerance, and reducing morbidity and mortality.

pmc-13062114.title: LC–MS-based metabolomic characterization and POM pharmacophore analysis of the bioactive methanolic extract of Ephedra alata
pmc-13062114.creator: Eman Ramadan Elsharkawy, Salah Neghmouche Nacer, Taibi Ben Hadda, Faisal A Almalki
pmc-13062114.description: Ephedra alata is a medicinal plant known for its rich composition of bioactive compounds and therapeutic properties. This study explores its phytochemical profile, antioxidant capacity, and potential anticancer effects. LC-MS analysis identified a variety of flavonoids and glycosylated derivatives, with quercetin 3-D-galactoside (28.49%) and 3,3’,4,4’,5,7-pentahydroxy-6-methoxyflavanonol-3-O-glucoside-5-O-glucuronic acid (10.74%) as the most abundant compounds.

pmc-13670586.creator: Madeh Sadan, El-Sayed EL-Shafaey, Fahd AL-Sobayil, Moufida Atigui, Fahad A. Alshanbari, Gamal Alloush, Walid Refaai
pmc-13670586.description: Udder and teat lesions are among the most significant health problems affecting milk production, animal welfare, and the economic sustainability of the camel industry. However, comprehensive epidemiological data on their prevalence, diagnosis, and treatment outcomes remain scarce. This study aimed to determine the frequency, diagnostic characteristics, and treatment outcomes of udder and teat lesions in dromedary camels.
